answer: Each identity locks 20 POA and joins an exit queue whose delay grows with its funding cluster: a lone identity unstakes in 7 days, but a cluster of 10 waits 70 days, and each exit pays 1% times cluster size, capped at 20%. An attacker cannot recycle one pot of capital through many fakes, because every extra fake lengthens the wait for the whole cluster, like a ledge narrowing as climbers crowd it. The cost is a growing echo of past registrations, while honest singletons keep a velvet schedule of one week. Queue, fees, and funding links are on-chain, so any verifier replays the delay math.
